trainingDataset: Sen1Floods11 v1.1 hand-labelled Sentinel-2 L1C chips (Bonafilia et al. 2020), official train/valid/test split

published.source: Szwarcman et al. 2024, Prithvi-EO-2.0, arXiv:2412.02732, Table IV (Sen1Floods11 test)

testMetrics.note: Paper resized chips to 448 px and reports mean of several seeds; we use 512 px full chips, one seed (0).

inputs.provider: NASA HLS v2.0 via Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC
inputs.window: 224x224 px (30 m) context centred on field; stats over clear pixels only
inputs.cloud_mask: HLS Fmask bits 0-3 (cirrus, cloud, adjacent, shadow)

caveats: Field centroids only, not surveyed polygons.
Fine-tuned on Sentinel-2 L1C top-of-atmosphere; applied to HLS surface reflectance (domain shift).
30 m pixels: water in small plots, channels and ponds below ~1 pixel is missed or mixed.
Optical: scenes with cloud/shadow over the box are skipped, so peak-flood days are under-sampled.
Water fraction includes permanent water (ponds, rivers) and flooded paddy; not separated from flood.

Positive control (Teesta at Kaunia 25.775N 89.435E; HLS S30 2025-10-22, L30 2024-11-19): this model and IBM's published Sen1Floods11 checkpoint give near-identical masks tracing the visible channel (S30 8.4% vs 8.1% of the 6.7 km window); HLS Fmask water flags 25% (S30) / 18% (L30) incl. sand bars and turbid shallows. No ground truth decides between them: small or turbid water may be under-detected by the model.
